close_reason: Qualifier_set field is intentionally stored but not yet used (v0.2). Added doc comment explaining this. Suppressor retain is correct.
description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:721–722

    #[allow(dead_code)]
    qualifier_set: Vec<x509_cert::ext::pkix::certpolicy::PolicyQualifierInfo>,

The field is suppressed with #[allow(dead_code)] because it is written but never read.  RFC 5280 §6.1 does not require propagating qualifiers through the policy state machine for validation purposes (qualifiers are informational); reading the field is legitimately out of scope for v0.1.

The concern is different: the field is typed as Vec<PolicyQualifierInfo> — a non-zero-sized always-allocated container.  If it is genuinely unused for v0.1 validation logic, the idiomatic approach is one of:

1. Type it as Vec<PolicyQualifierInfo> and document why it is carried (reserved for v0.2 output), or
2. Remove it entirely and re-add in v0.2 when it is actually used.

The current state — allocated, populated, #[allow(dead_code)] suppressed — is the worst of both worlds: it costs memory and CPU on every cert processed, and the allow(dead_code) suppresses a compiler signal that would help reviewers notice it.

At minimum the allow(dead_code) should be accompanied by a # Limitations rustdoc comment on the field explaining that qualifiers are carried but not currently surfaced in ValidatedPath.
title: PolicyNode qualifier_set: Vec not Option, but #[allow(dead_code)] hides unused field
